thread:
Aisha: Punting an idea: make offline package transfers resumable and allow prioritization of critical components (runtime, verifier) so nodes can boot earlier while remainder still streams. thoughts?
Tom: sounds useful. currently seed+delta is all-or-nothing for activation. partial activation causes mismatch in components and operator has to block traffic.
Diego: prioritization is interesting but introduces inter-component dependency graphs. we need a way to declare critical vs optional. maybe a component 'phase' field in manifest.
Rina: agree on phase field. Phase=1 (bootstrap), Phase=2 (models), Phase=3 (extras). operator can commit phase-by-phase.
Aisha: ok, but operator must guarantee compatibility between phases. e.g. runtime v2 + model v1 may break. propose a compatibility matrix in manifest or a required-min-phase list.
Tom: manifest snippet idea:
```
components:
  - id: runtime
    phase: 1
    requires: []
  - id: verifier
    phase: 1
    requires: [runtime]
  - id: base-model
    phase: 2
    requires: [runtime]
  - id: diagnostics
    phase: 3
    requires: []
```
Diego: with that we can stream phase 1, commit, then let node accept traffic, continue streaming phase 2. need a checkpointing protocol so partial streams can resume after reboots.
Rina: checkpointing: write per-component piece manifests to staging with offsets and chunk checksums. operator restarts read piece manifest and resume missing chunks. keep chunk size small (4-16MiB).
Aisha: for air-gapped setups, the transfer medium may be physical (USB). resumability still matters; use a component-level index file that the installer writes as it copies. agent can reconcile index vs target.
Tom: rollback story? what if phase2 fails verification after we already committed phase1? We have to ensure safe API surface when runtime upgrades first. maybe have a compatibility fallback: keep previous runtime binaries until all required phases verified, then perform final activation switch.
Diego: that looks like two-stage commit again: STAGED + ACTIVATED. STAGED can be per-phase. ACTIVATED flips the traffic. we should never remove previous runtime until ACTIVATED succeeded and a grace period passed.
Rina: add a garbage-collect policy with TTL and max-retain versions in CRD. default retain 1 previous. operator evicts old staged artifacts after retention.
Aisha: network optimization: prioritize small but critical components first. Idea: compute a criticality score and sort transfer queue. Also allow admin override for forced-phase ordering for emergency patches.
Tom: observability: events for chunk-received, chunk-verified, component-staged, component-committed, resume-start, resume-fail. Console timeline should show which phases are active and resume gaps.
Diego: security: index file must be signed and include component digests. installer/transfer tool signs pieces; node-agent verifies signature before resuming. prevents tampering in physical media.
Rina: edge case: mid-activation power loss while swapping runtime symlink. ensure swap is atomic: write new files to parallel path then symlink switch. prefer rename in same-fs. validate fs during preflight.
Aisha: pseudo protocol:
1) upload component manifest (signed)
2) transfer chunks with per-chunk checksum
3) write component index + offset metadata
4) verify full digest
5) set component state=STAGED
6) run component-specific smoke tests
7) if all required components in phase pass -> set phase=COMMITTED
8) if final phase committed -> ACTIVATED and old-version tombstone scheduled

Tom: what about operator leases to prevent concurrent activations? CRD should include activationLock with owner and expiration. prevent multiple controllers stomping.
Diego: good call. also add exponential backoff on resume attempts to avoid I/O storms on flaky media.
Rina: implement a small local reassembler that tolerates missing chunks and exposes a /status endpoint for progress. keeps UI friendly.
build-bot: build status: resumable-transfer-lib v0.2 uploaded to internal registry at 1809990018 :white_check_mark:
Aisha: I'll draft RFC with sample manifests, chunk layout, state machine diagram, and CRD fields: phases, retentionPolicy, activationLock, gcTTL, resumeBackoff. will include example USB and HTTP transfer flows.
Tom: please include a short admin checklist for emergency revert (force revert command + manual GC).
Diego: LGTM. small note: default chunk-size should be conservative (8MiB) and pluggable.
Rina: thanks everyone. I'll prototype the index format and share tests next week.
